response:
I fixed the WAL file and recovered all 11 records into `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id.

**What was wrong:** every byte of `main.db-wal` had been XORed with `0x42`. Long runs of `0x42` in the file, where zero bytes would normally be, gave it away. Undoing the XOR restored a valid WAL header (magic `0x377f0682`), and SQLite then read the WAL normally.

**Recovered data:**

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

Records 6–11 existed only in the WAL. The WAL also changed some of the original five (e.g. apple is 150 and banana is 250).

Opening the database with SQLite may have merged the WAL into `main.db` and removed the WAL file, so the WAL changes are now in `main.db` itself. Copies of the original encrypted WAL and database are in the container at `/tmp/wal.bak` and `/tmp/main.db.bak`.
